claims.text: multi-shop-data-rollout.md is a plan only at stage-4 (no migration or code in the repo); it carries out ADR 0013 over three releases, each leaving a schema the previous release's code still works with, so rolling back is deploying the version before.

Release 1: shops with today's shop as 1; shop_id integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1; foreign keys NOT VALID, validated in a separate migration; shop_id indexes and unique customers (shop_id, email) built CONCURRENTLY, suppressTransaction, lock_timeout; old unique on email kept.
Rollback of release 1: the code before it does not know the new columns, and every row it writes gets the default 1.

In PostgreSQL 17, ADD COLUMN with a non-volatile (e.g. constant) DEFAULT stores the value in the table's metadata and uses it for all existing rows, so no rewrite is required. It still takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, but does no per-row work, so it holds it only briefly once granted.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, ALTER TABLE, Notes (ADD COLUMN with non-volatile DEFAULT); 13.3.1 Table-Level Locks

claims.text: A foreign key added NOT VALID skips checking existing rows but is enforced for subsequent inserts and updates; VALIDATE CONSTRAINT later checks existing rows with a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, which does not block INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, ALTER TABLE: ADD table_constraint ... NOT VALID, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT; 13.3.1 Table-Level Locks

claims.text: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY lets writes continue and cannot run inside a transaction block; EF Core needs migrationBuilder.Sql with suppressTransaction: true for it; lock_timeout aborts a statement that waits longer than the limit to acquire a lock.
claims.source_hint: backend.l4.migration-locks summary lines 3-5; PostgreSQL 17 docs, CREATE INDEX (Building Indexes Concurrently), 19.11 lock_timeout; EF Core docs, Custom migration operations (suppressTransaction)

claims.text: Release 2: the shop comes from a shop_id claim Keycloak adds to the access token, not a client parameter; code writes and filters by shop_id; order.* and payment.* messages get optional shopId, readers use 1 when missing because old-shaped messages remain in outbox and queues.

Release 2 step 4: once every Pod runs release 2, a separate migration drops the shop_id default and the old unique index on email (replaced by customers (shop_id, email) from release 1). Before step 4 release 1 can be redeployed; after it, rollback only to release 2.
An INSERT that gives no value for a NOT NULL column with no default fails with a not-null constraint violation; with a default, the omitted column gets the default.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 5.2 Default Values; 5.5.2 Not-Null Constraints; INSERT

claims.text: Release 3: requests set app.shop_id with SET LOCAL; RLS on with a policy on shop_id = current_setting('app.shop_id', true)::integer; each service on its own non-superuser role without BYPASSRLS. Rollback: RLS off, old role back; code still filters.
An UPDATE locks each row it changes until its transaction ends; other UPDATE or DELETE of those rows waits.
ALTER TABLE ... SET NOT NULL checks every row by scanning the table (unless a valid CHECK constraint proves no NULL) and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, ALTER TABLE: SET/DROP NOT NULL and Notes on locking

claims.text: RLS policies do not apply to superusers or BYPASSRLS roles, and table owners normally bypass them too. In Compose the services connect as donhang, a superuser that owns the tables, so turning a policy on changes nothing for them.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 5.9 Row Security Policies; docker-compose.yml @ stage-4 (POSTGRES_USER donhang); db/tenancy/row-level-security.sql @ stage-4 line 5

claims.text: Under a role the policy applies to, a transaction that has not set app.shop_id does not see its shop's rows: current_setting('app.shop_id', true) gives no shop number to match.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 9.28.1 Configuration Settings Functions (current_setting missing_ok); 5.9 Row Security Policies

claims.text: On deploy, Argo CD runs the migration hook in wave 1 before the api Deployment in wave 2; the Deployment's rolling update (default maxSurge and maxUnavailable 25%, i.e. 1 and 0 for 2 replicas) then replaces the 2 api Pods one at a time.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs, Deployment rolling update (maxSurge, maxUnavailable); Argo CD docs, Sync Phases and Waves; deploy base/migrate-hook.yaml, base/api.yaml @ stage-4

claims.text: The plan assumes each Keycloak account belongs to one shop; if one account buys in several shops, the request's shop must come from elsewhere and release 2 must be reviewed.

When a table is small, its service can be stopped and the restarted version writes shop_id, one migration is acceptable; release 1 can ship while release 2 is redesigned; after the default is dropped, fix release 2 instead of redeploying release 1. Three releases cost three deploys.

shop_id goes to customers, orders, order_items, order_status_history, products (donhang), payments (donhang_payments), notifications (donhang_notifications); outbox/inbox tables get none; shops lives in donhang, other databases keep shop_id as a number with no foreign key.
SET LOCAL changes a setting only until the end of the current transaction; a custom setting with a dotted name such as app.shop_id can be set this way and read with current_setting.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SET (LOCAL); 19.16 Customized Options; 9.28.1 current_setting

beyond_scope: §6: one-migration plan's UPDATE row locks and SET NOT NULL scan, to answer misconception 1; no new mechanism beyond migration-locks.
